title: The Big Three meet at Tehran
pull: He moved in next door to Stalin

facts.text: The Tehran Conference, code named Eureka, ran from 28 November to 1 December 1943. It was the first time Franklin D. Roosevelt, Winston Churchill and Joseph Stalin met together.

At 9:30 a.m. on 28 November, Stalin sent word through Ambassador Averell Harriman that he was worried about the distance between the American Legation, where Roosevelt was staying, and the Soviet Embassy, because Tehran was full of Axis sympathizers.

Harriman told the President that if he kept refusing quarters in the Soviet compound, the Americans would be responsible for any harm to Stalin driving across the city. Tehran had been under complete German control only months before. Roosevelt accepted the Soviet invitation.

At 3:00 p.m. Roosevelt, Admiral William Leahy, Harry Hopkins and Major John Boettiger drove to the Soviet Embassy to live there as guests of the Soviet government. Stalin lived in a smaller house in the same compound, and the British Legation was a block away.
To keep up the impression that the President was still at the American Legation, Admirals Wilson Brown and Ross McIntire and General Edwin Watson went back there after seeing him settled.
At 3:15 p.m. Stalin called on Roosevelt, their first meeting ever. The President greeted him: "I am glad to see you. I have tried for a long time to bring this about."
The first plenary meeting opened at 4:00 p.m. in the Soviet Embassy. Roosevelt, as the youngest of the three, said he ventured to welcome his elders.
Generals George Marshall and Henry Arnold missed that first meeting. It had been called at very short notice, and both were out on an auto tour of Tehran.
Stalin argued that Italy was no road to the heart of Germany. The best way, he said, was an attack through northern or northwestern France, though the Germans would fight like devils to stop it.
Stalin also told the meeting that once Germany was beaten, the Soviet Union would reinforce Siberia, "and then we shall be able by our common front to beat Japan."

The payoff: before the conference ended, the British and Americans committed to Operation Overlord, the invasion of northern France, by May 1944, and the Soviets agreed to a major offensive in the east to hold German troops away from it.
Roosevelt stayed at the Soviet Embassy to the end. He left it at 10:30 p.m. on 1 December for the U.S. Army's Camp Amirabad, and flew back to Cairo on 2 December.

Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill seated on the portico of the Soviet Embassy, Tehran, with Arnold, Brooke, Cunningham, Leahy and others standing behind; close, sharp, faces fill the frame. NARA 342-FH-3A48363 (U.S. Air Force number 60744AC), NAID 204998903, from a 4x5 print received December 1944 from the Signal Corps Photo Library, stamped Released for Publication, BPR. Use Unrestricted, U.S. government work, public domain. Cropped from the 4576 x 3551 scan of the mount (border, punch holes, handwriting and the number A48363 removed; the printed 60744 A.C. at lower right was cropped out), saved 1920 x 1520. NARA dates it only to the conference, 28 November to 1 December 1943; the portico photos are generally dated 29 November, so the credit says November 1943. Runner up: the wider portico view 342-FH-3A48361 (NAID 204998856, Signal Corps 183219), same sitting with the columns.

declassified.fact: The day was also payday for losing bets. The Navy had beaten Army 13 to 0 at football the day before, and the President's log records that General Watson spent 28 November paying up his many football bets to nearly everyone in the party. That night Roosevelt's Filipino mess staff cooked the dinner for Stalin and Churchill in an empty room at the Soviet Embassy, where ranges had to be installed first.

NOON: 02:20 to 03:00, Stalin, Roosevelt and Churchill seated on the portico with staff behind, photographers in the foreground, the close shot of the three at 02:44 to 02:49 (open on it or on the wide shot at 02:22); 03:00 to 03:06 they rise; 03:06 park shot, then white leader. film.license: NARA use status Unrestricted (FDR Library Motion Pictures collection). Silent compilation with the same intertitle lettering and many of the same shots as the U.S. Army Signal Corps conference reels (111-ADC-310, 111-ADC-1015), so it is treated as U.S. government film, public domain.
film.date_note: Filmed during the conference, 28 November to 1 December 1943; the portico sitting is generally dated 29 November, the day after the opening. The caption should say film from the Tehran Conference, not film of 28 November.
